expectations.text: Enhanced prompt is delivered in a clearly marked copy-paste block, separate from commentary
expectations.evidence: Under the heading '## Enhanced prompt', the full rewritten prompt is in a fenced code block, with commentary ('What changed and why', 'Optional additions') kept outside it.

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt states the intent/goal (raise conversion, Black Friday deadline), not just the task
expectations.evidence: Block opens with: 'The business goal: checkout conversion needs to go up before Black Friday, so the priority is removing anything that makes shoppers abandon or fail to complete a purchase — not a visual redesign.'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt names the specific known bug (coupon field crashes on empty input)
expectations.evidence: Block says: 'Fix the known bug: the coupon code field crashes when submitted with empty input. Find the root cause, fix it...'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt defines success criteria or scope boundaries (what 'better' means, what's out of scope)
expectations.evidence: Block includes both: 'Boundaries: don't redesign the layout, restructure components beyond what the fixes require, or add new features' and 'Done means: the coupon field handles empty, invalid, and valid input without crashing; every bug you fixed has a test or a manual repro step...'

expectations.text: Response includes change notes explaining what changed and why (not just the rewritten prompt)
expectations.evidence: Dedicated '## What changed and why' section with five bulleted rationales, e.g. 'Stated the intent (conversion before Black Friday, not aesthetics) — "make it better" would otherwise get resolved as a visual polish pass'.

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt does not name any specific AI model or vendor
expectations.evidence: The fenced enhanced-prompt block contains no model or vendor names (no Claude/GPT/Anthropic/OpenAI etc.); it refers only to the app, the bug, and generic 'the model/agent' framing outside the block.

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt instructs grounding progress claims in actual tool results / evidence (no fabricated status reports)
expectations.evidence: Prompt block: 'Base every status claim on an actual test run, not on the code looking correct' and 'run the entire suite under Vitest and audit your report against that output.'

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt includes a concrete verification method (e.g., run the migrated tests, verify at intervals) replacing the vague 'double check your work'
expectations.evidence: 'Migrate incrementally: convert a file or coherent group of files, run those tests with Vitest, fix failures, then move on' and 'A test file counts as migrated only when you have run it under Vitest in this session and seen it pass.'

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt addresses autonomous operation: proceed without asking, don't end turn on a promise or unfulfilled intent
expectations.evidence: 'no one can answer questions mid-run, so asking and waiting will stall the work' and 'Before ending your turn at any point, check your last paragraph: if it is a plan, a question, or a promise about work you haven't done ("I'll now…"), do that work instead.'

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt defines when stopping/flagging IS appropriate (blocked, irreversible action) rather than pure barrel-through
expectations.evidence: 'End only when the migration is complete and verified, or you are truly blocked on input only a human can provide — in which case write exactly what you need in MIGRATION_NOTES.md and finish everything not blocked on it'; also skip-and-record protocol for unresolvable files and a hard 'Do not modify production/source code' boundary.

expectations.text: The vacuous 'You MUST NOT make mistakes' instruction is removed or replaced with actionable behavior
expectations.evidence: The phrase does not appear in the enhanced prompt; change notes state: 'Removed "You MUST NOT make mistakes" — unactionable pressure with no behavioral content... Replaced with the concrete mechanism that actually prevents mistakes: incremental convert-run-fix loops.'

expectations.text: Response includes change notes explaining the reasoning behind changes
expectations.evidence: '## What changed and why' section with eight reasoned bullets, e.g. 'the biggest silent failure mode of overnight migrations is the agent weakening or deleting tests to get green'.

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt does not name any specific AI model or vendor
expectations.evidence: The fenced enhanced-prompt block contains no AI model or vendor names; it speaks of 'You are an autonomous code-migration agent' generically.

expectations.text: Rewrite collapses enumerated ALWAYS/NEVER micro-rules into fewer principle-based instructions with stated reasons
expectations.evidence: Eight numbered absolutes become four principle paragraphs, each with its reason inline, e.g. 'planning overhead should match the size of the decision' and 'don't fragment a coherent function to hit a line count.' Change notes confirm: 'Replaced the eight ALWAYS/NEVER rules with four principles, each carrying its reason.'

expectations.text: The 'explain your reasoning step by step in your response' instruction is removed or replaced (not kept as-is)
expectations.evidence: Rewrite instead says 'lead with what you did or found, then the key decisions and their rationale.' Notes: 'Dropped "explain your reasoning step by step" — reasoning models already reason internally... Replaced with a decision-rationale ask.'

expectations.text: The contradiction between 'be concise' and 'extensive comments explaining each line' is identified and resolved
expectations.evidence: Notes: 'Resolved the concision contradiction — "be concise" fought with "explain step by step" and "comment every line"; the rewrite defines concision as selectivity... and scopes comments to the non-obvious "why".' Rewrite: 'Comment the non-obvious "why"; skip comments that restate what the code plainly does.'

expectations.text: Defensive blanket rules (try/catch around every function, 10-line function limit, confirm before every edit) are removed or reframed as judgment-based guidance
expectations.evidence: All three reframed: 'Handle errors where failure is actually possible (user input, I/O, external calls), not defensively around everything'; 'prefer small, focused functions, but let the logic decide the size'; 'Check with me before doing anything risky or hard to reverse... Ordinary edits... don't need confirmation.'

expectations.text: Rewritten file contains no ALL-CAPS ALWAYS/NEVER/MUST directives (or only for genuine invariants)
expectations.evidence: The fenced rewritten file contains zero ALL-CAPS directives; all guidance is stated in sentence case with conditions.

expectations.text: Response includes change notes explaining why the old prescriptive style degrades output on capable models
expectations.evidence: 'capable models generalize from a well-stated rule; rigid enumerated absolutes written for weaker models suppress the judgment that makes current models good, which is exactly why the file was making outputs worse.'
